lastPrompt: This is the Machine Learning Practical (MLP) coursework framework used in an introductory deep-learning course. It provides a NumPy-based neural network library (`mlp` package) for building and training neural networks from scratch. Multiple core modules have been left unimplemented and must be completed so that all tests pass. Your working directory is `/workspace`. The project code is already present at `/workspace/mlp/`. Implement the following modules: The following modules need to be implemented or substantially built out: layers (`mlp/layers.py`): Neural network layer implementations including affine (fully connected) transformations, activation functions (sigmoid, ReLU, leaky ReLU, ELU, SELU, tanh, softmax), radial basis function projections, dropout, reshape, batch normalization, and 2D convolution. In addition to the forward/backward passes, this task now also hollows constructor and parameter-interface logic for the affine, batch-normalization, convolution, RBF, dropout, leaky-ReLU, ELU, SELU, and reshape layers where those interfaces are exercised by the tests. (~52 functions / interfaces to implement) errors (`mlp/errors.py`): Scalar error (loss) functions used to train models, including sum-of-squared-differences, binary cross-entropy, binary cross-entropy with sigmoid, multi-class cross-entropy, and cross-entropy with softmax. Each error function requires both a forward evaluation method and a gradient method. (~10 functions to implement) learning_rules (`mlp/learning_rules.py`): Gradient-based parameter update rules including base gradient-descent parameter initialisation/update handling, constructor-level hyperparameter validation/storage, momentum SGD, RMSProp, and Adam. The adaptive rules must also initialise and reset their optimizer state in addition to performing in-place parameter updates, and Momentum now also hollows its reset path. (~15 functions / interfaces to implement) models (`mlp/models.py`): The single-layer and multi-layer model classes which store their wrapped layer(s), proxy wrapped-layer parameters/gradients, orchestrate forward propagation through a sequence of layers, expose a flattened `params` view over all parameterised layers, and compute gradients with respect to all model parameters via backpropagation. (~8 functions / interfaces to implement) optimisers (`mlp/optimisers.py`): The training-loop optimiser that wires models, error functions, learning rules, and datasets together. It must initialise the learning rule from model parameters, execute batched training epochs, evaluate monitor metrics, aggregate per-epoch statistics, log them, and return full run statistics. (~6 functions / interfaces to implement) The tests also depend on these signatures and entry points: The following functions are called directly by the test suite.
